subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a core pace-aware provider quota policy, and should autonomous agent behavior be advisory-only or blocking?
rationale: This choice affects provider contracts, auth-profile/session state, new config, persisted runtime state, status/tool output, and autonomous dispatch policy, so cleanup automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Advisory Pace Visibility First
options.body: Add provider-owned pace metadata and status/session_status visibility without default blocking, then evaluate opt-in throttling after real usage evidence.

options.title: Opt-In Blocking Guardrail
options.body: Design explicit config-gated throttling with persisted state and tests for subagent and non-interactive behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep Outside Core For Now
options.body: Route experimentation to a plugin, skill, or external operator tool until a generic provider contract is proven necessary.

recommendation.title: Advisory Pace Visibility First
recommendation.body: Add provider-owned pace metadata and status/session_status visibility without default blocking, then evaluate opt-in throttling after real usage evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provider-usage feature history and the product/API scope make steipete the best available routing owner among the identified history signals.
